The commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Karim) on Surah 89, verse 1:

It has been my custom to speak, by God's grace, on the interpretation (tafsir) of the Noble Qur'an, which we began with Surah An-Naba', and we have now reached Surah Al-Fajr. So we say, and in God we trust: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿By the dawn, (1) and by ten nights, (2) and by the even and the odd, (3) and by the night when it passes, (4)﴾ [Al-Fajr 1-4]. All of these are oaths: by ﴿al-fajr﴾ (the dawn), ﴿layalin 'ashr﴾ (ten nights), ﴿al-shaf'​﴾ (the even), ﴿al-witr﴾ (the odd), and ﴿al-layl idha yasr﴾ (the night when it passes). These are five things by which Allah the Exalted swore.

The first: ﴿al-fajr﴾ (the dawn). The fajr is the bright light that appears on the eastern horizon shortly before sunrise. The time between it and sunrise is between one hour and thirty-two minutes and one hour and seventeen minutes, and it varies with the seasons. That is, sometimes the interval between dawn and sunrise is long, and sometimes it is short, according to the seasons.

There are two dawns: the true dawn (fajr sadiq) and the false dawn (fajr kadhib). The intended meaning of fajr here is the true dawn. The difference between the true and false dawn is in three respects:

The first aspect: the false dawn appears elongated in the sky, not spread horizontally but vertically. The true dawn, however, spreads horizontally, extending from north to south.

The second difference: after the true dawn there is no darkness; rather, the light increases until the sun rises. As for the false dawn, darkness follows it after this light appears. For this reason it is called "false," because it fades away and disappears.

The third difference: the true dawn is joined to the horizon, whereas between the false dawn and the horizon there is darkness.

These are three visible differences that people can recognize when they are in the open country. In cities, however, they do not recognize them, because the lights obscure these signs.

Allah swore by the dawn because it is the beginning of the day, and it is in reality a transition from thick darkness to a bright dawn. Allah also swore by it because no one can bring about this dawn except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Say: "Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not listen?"﴾ [Al-Qasas 71].

Allah also swore by the dawn because legal rulings depend on it, such as the fasting person's abstention. When dawn breaks, the fasting person must abstain, whether his fast is obligatory or voluntary (nafl), if he wishes to complete his fast. Also dependent on it is the entry of the time of the dawn prayer. These are two great legal rulings, and the more important of them is the entry of the prayer time. That is, we must be more careful about the dawn for the sake of the entry of the prayer time than we are for the sake of abstaining during fasting. Why? Because if we make a mistake in abstaining from what breaks the fast, we have acted on a basis, which is that the night still remains. But in prayer, if we err and pray before dawn, we have not acted on a basis, because the basis is that the night remains and the prayer time has not entered. For this reason, if a person prays the dawn prayer one minute before its time enters, his prayer is a voluntary prayer (nafl) and it does not clear his obligation (dhimmah). Therefore, brothers, we call your attention to this matter, namely taking care of the entry of the dawn prayer time, because many muezzins call the adhan before dawn, and this is an error, since calling the adhan before the time is not prescribed. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the prayer is due, let one of you call the adhan for you."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (628) and Muslim (674/292), from the hadith of Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

When does the prayer become due? I ask you.

* Students: When its time enters.

* The Shaykh: When its time has entered. If a person calls the adhan before the prayer time enters, his adhan is not valid, and he must repeat it. Care regarding the entry of dawn is very important for observing the prayer time.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 89, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And by the ten nights﴾. It has been said: the intended meaning of "the ten nights" is the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, and "nights" is applied to the days because the Arabic language is broad; "nights" may be used while days are intended, and "days" may be used while nights are intended. And it has been said: the intended meaning of "the ten nights" is the last ten nights of Ramadan.

As for the first view, those who say the intended meaning of "the ten nights" is the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, it is because the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah are excellent days, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said about them: "There are no days on which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days." They said: not even jihad in the way of Allah? He said: "Not even jihad in the way of Allah, except a man who goes out with his self and his wealth and does not return with anything of that."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2438) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]

As for those who said the intended meaning is the last ten nights of Ramadan, they said: the original meaning of "nights" is actually nights, not days. They said: the last ten nights of Ramadan include the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), about which Allah said that it is ﴿better than a thousand months﴾ [al-Qadr 3], and He said it is blessed, and He said: ﴿in it every wise matter is decreed﴾ [al-Dukhan 4]. This view is stronger than the first view, although the first view is the view of the majority (al-jumhur). But the wording does not support the majority view, while what favors the second view is that they are the last ten nights of Ramadan, and Allah swore by them for their nobility, and because the Night of Decree is in them, and because Muslims conclude with them the month of Ramadan, which is the time of an obligation among the obligations of Islam and the pillars of Islam. Therefore Allah swore by these nights.

Regarding His saying, ﴿By the even and the odd﴾, it has been said that what is meant is all of creation: all of creation is either even or odd, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, ﴿And of everything We have created pairs﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 49]. Acts of worship are either even or odd, so what is meant by the even and the odd is everything created as even or odd, and everything legislated as even or odd.

It has also been said that what is meant by the even is all of creation, and what is meant by the odd is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Know that His saying ﴿and the odd﴾ has two sound recitations: ﴿al-witr﴾ with a kasra on the waw (وِتْر) and ﴿al-watr﴾ with a fatha on the waw (وَتْر). That is, if you recite ﴿wal-shaf'i wal-witr﴾ it is valid, and if you recite ﴿wal-shaf'i wal-watr﴾ it is also valid. Those who said that the even is creation reasoned that all created things are composed of two things, ﴿And of everything We have created pairs﴾, and that the odd (watr or witr) is Allah, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): «Indeed Allah is odd (witr) and loves the odd»[[Narrated by Muslim (2677 / 5) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. When a verse can bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, then it should carry all the meanings it can bear. This is a principle in the science of tafsir: when a verse can bear two meanings and one of them does not negate the other, it is to be understood as encompassing both meanings together.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And by the night when it passes﴾. Allah swears also by the night when it travels on. As-Sura (ٱلسُّرَى) is travelling at night, and the night, as we know, travels: it begins at maghrib and ends with the break of dawn. It goes on, moving for a period of time without stopping, always in motion. Allah swore by it because of the acts of worship performed in its hours, such as the maghrib and 'isha' prayers, qiyam al-layl (night prayer), witr, and others. Moreover, the night has a great occasion, namely that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and says: "Who is calling upon Me that I may respond to him? Who is asking Me that I may give to him? Who is seeking My forgiveness that I may forgive him?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1145) and Muslim (758 / 168), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] For this reason we say that the last third of the night is a time of answered supplication, so a person should seize this opportunity, stand before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in night prayer (tahajjud), and supplicate Allah, Glorified and Exalted, for whatever good of this world and the Hereafter he wishes, perhaps he will coincide with a moment of response from which he benefits in his worldly life and his Hereafter. Let us limit ourselves to this (...).

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and I send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, the seal of the prophets, and upon his family and companions and all who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the sixty-third session, or rather the sixty-third meeting of the meetings held every Thursday of each week. This Thursday is the twenty-eighth of the month of Muharram in the year 1415 AH. We begin this meeting with what we are accustomed to, namely the explanation of some of the noble verses of Allah, where our discussion ended at the words of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Is there not in that an oath for one of sense?﴾ [al-Fajr 5].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, [6] Iram, of the pillars?﴾ [al-Fajr 6-7]. The address here is to everyone to whom this Mighty Book is directed, which is all of mankind, and the jinn as well.

﴿Have you not considered﴾, O addressee, ﴿how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, [6] Iram, of the pillars﴾, meaning: what He did to them. 'Ad is a well-known tribe in the south of the Arabian Peninsula. Allah the Exalted sent Hud, upon him be prayers and peace, to them, and he conveyed the message to them, but they became arrogant, transgressed, and said: "Who is stronger than us in strength?" Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is greater than them in strength? And they were rejecting Our signs﴾ [Fussilat 15]. So they boasted of their strength, but Allah showed that they are weak before the strength of Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them﴾, and He did not say "that Allah is stronger than them in strength," but rather said ﴿who created them﴾, to show their weakness and that He, may He be glorified and exalted, is stronger than them, because the Creator is stronger than the created. ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is greater than them in strength? And they were rejecting Our signs (15). So We sent upon them a furious wind during days of misfortune to make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped﴾ [Fussilat 15-16].

Here He says: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad﴾: what He did to them was that He sent upon them the barren wind, ﴿which He imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen as though they were hollow trunks of palm trees﴾ [al-Haqqah 7], and ﴿by morning nothing was seen except their dwellings﴾ [al-Ahqaf 25]. This interrogative, by which Allah draws attention to what He did to these people, is intended to produce reflection; meaning: take heed, O you who deny the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), of how these were made to taste this punishment. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 83].

His saying ﴿Iram﴾: this is a description of the tribe. It was also said to be the name of a city, and other things were said. Whether it is the name of a tribe or the name of a city, Allah the Exalted punished them with a great punishment, even though they were strong.

His saying ﴿of the pillars (7), the like of which was not created in the lands﴾ [al-Fajr 7-8] means: people of the pillars, that is, strong buildings. ﴿The like of which was not created in the lands﴾: meaning, the like of it was not built in the lands, because they were strong and well-constructed. This is what deceived them, and they said: "Who is stronger than us in strength?"

In His saying ﴿the like of which was not created in the lands﴾, although it was man who built them, there is evidence that man may be described with the word "creating," as one says: "he created such-and-such." From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) about the painters: "It will be said to them: Give life to what you have created" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5951), Muslim (2108/97), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both]. But the creating attributed to people, indeed the creating attributed to the created, is not the creating attributed to Allah. The creating attributed to Allah is bringing into existence after non-existence, and transformation and change; whereas the creating attributed to other than Allah is merely transformation and change. Let me give you an example: this door is of wood. Who created the wood? Allah. No human can create it. But a human can transform the trunks and branches of wood into doors, into cabinets, and the like. So the creating attributed to the created is not the creating attributed to the Creator. Do you understand the difference? Answer.

* Student: Transformation; the creating attributed..

* Shaykh: The creating attributed to the Creator is bringing into being from non-existence, which no one can do; while what is attributed to the created is change and transformation, transforming a thing from one attribute to another. As for changing the essences, meaning making gold into silver, or silver into iron, or the like, this is impossible and can be done by none but Allah alone, without partner.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and I send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, the seal of the prophets, and upon his family and companions and all who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

Then He said: ﴿And Thamud, who hewed out the rocks in the valley﴾ [Al-Fajr 9]. (Thamud) are the people of Salih, and their dwellings are known today, as the Exalted said: ﴿The companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers﴾ [Al-Hijr 80], in the surah ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾ [Al-Hijr 1]. Allah mentioned that Thamud lived in the land of al-Hijr, and it is well known. The Prophet ﷺ passed by it on his way to Tabuk and hastened, and he covered his head ﷺ and said: "Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping, lest there befall you what befell them"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4702) and Muslim (2980 / 38), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. These people, Allah had given them strength, so that they would hew out the mountains, the gravel, and the great rocks; they would carve them and make houses from them. Therefore He said: ﴿who hewed out the rocks in the valley﴾, meaning the valley of Thamud, which is well known. Allah also inflicted upon them the punishment and retribution He inflicted; it was said to them: "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days" [Hud 65]. Then, after the three days, the Blast and the Quake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homes in the morning.

So it is incumbent upon us, brothers, to take a lesson from the state of these deniers whose end was destruction and ruin. And it should be known that this Ummah will not be destroyed by what the previous nations were destroyed by, namely this general punishment, for the Prophet ﷺ "asked Allah, the Exalted, that He not destroy them with a general famine"[[Narrated by Muslim (2889 / 19), from the hadith of Thawban, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. However, this Ummah may be destroyed by Allah making their violence (ba's) among themselves, so wars and fighting break out between them, and some of them are destroyed at the hands of others, not by something sent down from the heavens as Allah the Exalted did to the previous nations. Therefore it is obligatory upon us to beware of trials, whether apparent or hidden, and to keep away from everything that stirs people against one another, and to always adhere to calm, and to keep away from idle talk (qil wa qal) and excessive questioning, for that is among what the Prophet ﷺ forbade[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1477) and Muslim (593 / 12), from the hadith of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden you disobedience to mothers, burying daughters alive, and withholding and demanding (from people); and He disliked for you three things: qil and qal, excessive questioning, and squandering of wealth."]]. How many a single word has done what the sharp swords do! So the duty is to beware of trials, and that we be a united and mutually loving Ummah, where each of us seeks excuses for his brother when he sees from him what he dislikes. We ask Allah to grant us all success in what is good and righteous, and to unite our hearts upon His obedience.

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, [the people of] Iram of the pillars, the like of whom was not created in the lands? And Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley?﴾ [al-Fajr 6-9].

He says: ﴿And Pharaoh, the possessor of stakes﴾ [al-Fajr 10]. Pharaoh is the one to whom Allah sent Musa, peace and blessings be upon him. He had subjugated the Children of Israel in Egypt, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive.

The scholars have differed concerning the reason that led him to this ugly deed: why did he kill the sons and spare the women? Some scholars said: his soothsayers told him that a man would be born among the Children of Israel who would bring about his destruction at his hands, so he began killing the sons and sparing the women. Among the scholars is one who said: he did this in order to weaken the Children of Israel, because when a people's men are killed and their women are spared, they are undoubtedly humiliated. The first is the explanation of the people of transmitted reports (ahl al-athar), and the second is the explanation of the people of reasoning (ahl al-nazar), i.e., the people of intellect. It is not far-fetched that both matters became causes for this act, but by the power of Allah, mighty and majestic, the man whose hand would bring about Pharaoh's destruction was raised in the very house of Pharaoh, for Pharaoh's wife took him up and raised him in Pharaoh's house.

Pharaoh was arrogant in the land and exalted himself in the land, and he said to his people: ﴿I am your lord, the Most High﴾ [al-Nazi'at 24], and he said to them: ﴿I know of no god for you other than myself﴾ [al-Qasas 38], and he said to them: ﴿Am I not better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly express himself?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 52], meaning Musa. Allah Most High said: ﴿So he made his people feeble-minded, and they obeyed him﴾ [al-Zukhruf 54]. And you know that he said to his people, affirming to them: ﴿Does not the dominion of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Will you not then see?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 51]. He boasted of the rivers, which are water, and so he was drowned by water.

﴿And Pharaoh, the possessor of stakes﴾: that is, the possessor of strength, because his soldiers were to him like the stake (watad), and the stake, as we know, is what the ropes of a tent are tied to so that it stays firm and steady. So he had armies, great nations of sorcerers, soothsayers and others. But Allah, glorified and exalted, is above everything.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who transgressed in the lands﴾ [Al-Fajr 11]. At-Tughyan (transgression) means going beyond the limit. From it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship﴾ [Al-Haqqah 11]. That is: when the water rose beyond its measure, We carried you in the sailing ship, meaning the ship that Nuh (peace be upon him) built. So the meaning of ﴿transgressed in the lands﴾ is: they exceeded their bounds and oppressed the servants of Allah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 89, verse 12:

﴿So they increased corruption therein﴾ [al-Fajr 89:12]. Is the corruption (al-fasad) the corruption that is perceptible (al-hissi) or the corruption that is moral (al-ma'nawi)?

The answer: It is the moral corruption, and moral corruption is followed by perceptible corruption. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth; but they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn﴾ [al-A'raf 7:96]. For this reason some of the scholars said, concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order﴾ [al-A'raf 7:56], they said: "Do not corrupt it through acts of disobedience." Based on this, His saying ﴿they increased corruption therein﴾ means the moral corruption, but moral corruption is followed by perceptible corruption. Among the nations before, Allah the Exalted would utterly destroy these deniers, every last one of them. But Allah lifted this type of punishment from this Ummah and made its punishment that their violence be directed among themselves: they destroy one another among themselves. Based on this, what has occurred among the Muslims of fighting one another and destroying one another is due to what cause? Its cause is sins and transgressions. Allah sets some of them over others, and this is a punishment from Allah, glorified and exalted is He. For this reason He said: ﴿So they increased corruption therein (12). So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment﴾ [al-Fajr 89:12-13].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 89, verse 13:

﴿Then your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.﴾ The word ﴿ṣabba﴾ (poured, cast down): ṣabb is well known to be from above, and the punishment that came upon these people came from above, from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

And ﴿sawṭa ʿadhāb﴾ (a scourge of punishment): the sawṭ is the staff with which one strikes, and it is known that striking with a staff is a kind of punishment. But is this scourge that Allah, exalted is He, poured upon ʿĀd, Thamūd and Pharaoh the staff that we know, or is it a staff of punishment that destroyed them?

The answer: the second. It is a staff of punishment that destroyed them and annihilated them. We ask Allah, exalted is He, to make for us and for you in the nations that passed before us a lesson by which we take heed and benefit, and to make us obedient to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not transgressors. Indeed He is over all things capable. And may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and upon his family and all his companions.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the sixty-fifth session of the weekly lesson held every Thursday. This is Thursday, the thirteenth of the month of Safar, in the year one thousand four hundred and fifteen (after the Hijrah).

Today's session will be on the explanation of verses from Surah al-Fajr, where we stopped at the words of Allah, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment﴾ [al-Fajr 13].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [al-Fajr 14]. The address here is to the Prophet (ﷺ) or to everyone to whom the address is directed. Allah, may He be exalted, makes clear that He is "watchful" (bi-l-mirsad) over everyone who transgresses, oversteps, and is arrogant: He is watching him, and He will punish him and call him to account. This meaning has parallels in the Noble Qur'an, among them the saying of Allah, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers there are similar [fates]﴾ [Muhammad 10]; and like the saying of Shu'ayb to his people: ﴿Lest there befall you the like of what befell the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih; and the people of Lot are not far from you﴾ [Hud 89]. So the way (sunnah) of Allah, glorified and exalted, is one and the same toward those who deny His messengers and are arrogant toward worshipping Him: He is watchful over them. This verse conveys a warning and threat to whoever is arrogant toward worshipping Allah or denies His report.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 89, verses 15–16:

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him by honouring him and bestowing blessings upon him, he says, "My Lord has honoured me." But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."﴾ [al-Fajr 15–16]

Trial (ibtila') from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, comes through both good and evil, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial.﴾ [al-Anbiya' 35]. Man is tested with good so that Allah may see whether he gives thanks or disbelieves, and he is tested with evil so that He may see whether he is patient or transgresses. The states of man, as you all know, revolve between good and evil: between good that suits him and gladdens him, and evil that does not suit him and does not gladden him. All of it is a trial from Allah.

Man, by his human nature, which is built upon wrongdoing and ignorance, when his Lord tests him by honouring him and bestowing blessings upon him, says: ﴿My Lord has honoured me.﴾ That is, "I am deserving of honour," and he does not acknowledge the grace of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "I was only given it on account of knowledge I have."﴾ [al-Qasas 78]. When he was reminded of Allah's blessing upon him, he said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I have,﴾ and he did not acknowledge the grace of Allah. How many people there are whose state is like this: when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, honours them and bestows blessings upon them, they say, "This is an honour from Allah to us, because we are deserving of it." If a person said, "Allah has honoured me with such-and-such," acknowledging His grace and speaking of His blessing, there would be no harm in that for him. But if he says, "I have been honoured," meaning, "I am deserving of honour," it is like when the chief of a people, upon a guest's arrival at one of their homes, says, "So-and-so has honoured me, because I am deserving of it."

﴿And as for when He tests him by restricting his provision﴾ meaning, He constricts his provision for him, ﴿he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."﴾ meaning, no; he says that Allah, the Exalted, has wronged him and humiliated him, and has not provided for him as He provided for so-and-so, nor honoured him as He honoured so-and-so. Thus, in ease he does not give thanks, he is self-admiring and says, "This is my right," and in hardship he does not endure patiently, but rather objects to his Lord and says: ﴿My Lord has humiliated me.﴾ This is the state of man insofar as he is a human being. As for the believer, it is not so. When Allah honours him and bestows blessings upon him, the believer thanks his Lord for that and regards it as a grace and kindness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and not as an honour owed to its recipient as though he were entitled to it. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, tests him and restricts his provision, he endures patiently, seeks reward, and says: "This is because of my sin, and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has not humiliated me or wronged me." Thus he is patient in affliction and thankful in ease.

In the two verses there is an indication that a person must reflect and say, for example: Why has Allah given me wealth? What does He want from me? He wants me to give thanks. Why has Allah afflicted me with poverty, with illness, and the like? He wants me to be patient. Let him therefore be one who holds himself to account, so that he does not become like the state of man, which is built upon ignorance and wrongdoing.

Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nay﴾ [Al-Fajr 17], meaning: He did not give you what He gave you as an honour to you, because you deserve it, but it is an act of grace from Him. And He did not humiliate you when He restricted your provision; rather, this is the requirement of His wisdom and justice.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nay, but you do not honour the orphan﴾ [Al-Fajr 17], meaning: when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has honoured you with blessings, you do not show kindness to those who deserve to be honoured, namely the orphans. Here "al-yatim" (the orphan) is a generic noun, not referring to one particular orphan but to the category of orphans. The scholars said that the yatim (orphan) is one whose father died before reaching puberty, whether male or female. As for one whose mother has died, he is not an orphan.

He says: ﴿Nay, but you do not honour the orphan﴾. Allah's words ﴿the orphan﴾ include the poor among orphans and the wealthy, meaning that even a wealthy orphan deserves kindness and honour, because his heart has been broken by the loss of his father and of the one who attended to his affairs. Therefore Allah the Exalted enjoined kindness towards him until this brokenness that has afflicted him is removed.

Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 89, verse 18:

﴿And do not urge one another to feed the poor﴾ [al-Fajr: 18]. That is: none of you urges another to feed the needy. And if one does not urge others, he also does not do it himself; so he neither feeds the poor nor urges the feeding of the poor. In this there is an indication that we ought to honour orphans, and that some of us should urge one another to feed the needy, because they are in need. And Allah, the Exalted, is in the aid of the servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 89, verse 19:

﴿And you devour the heritage, devouring it greedily (19). And you love wealth with an intense love (20).﴾ [al-Fajr: 19, 20].

﴿Al-turath (the heritage)﴾ is what Allah bestows upon the servant of wealth, whether he inherits it from a deceased person, or he buys, sells and earns it, or he goes out to the desert and brings back what he brings of grass and firewood and other things. The point is that al-turath is what a person inherits, or what Allah bestows upon a person of wealth, for the children of Adam devour it greedily.

And as for wealth, Allah says: ﴿And you love wealth with immense love﴾, i.e., greatly. This is the nature of man. But faith has its effects: a person, by his faith, may not be concerned with wealth; if it comes, he thanks Allah for it and fulfils what is obligatory upon him, and if it goes, he is not concerned about it. However, human nature, as such, is as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, described it in these two verses. We ask Allah, exalted is He, to grant us and you success in what is good and righteous, and to protect us from the evil of our own souls. Verily, He is over all things Competent.

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the last meeting in the month of Safar of the year 1415 AH, from the meeting known as (Liqa al-Bab al-Maftuh) (the Open Door Meeting), which takes place every Thursday of the week. This day is the twenty-seventh of Safar. It has been our custom to speak on the tafsir (exegesis) of some of the verses of Allah, and we had reached His statement, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Nay, when the earth is pounded to powder, pounded and pounded (21), and your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank (22), and Hell is brought near that Day; on that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance benefit him? (23)﴾ [Al-Fajr 21-23]. So Allah, glorified and exalted, reminds people of the Day of Resurrection: ﴿when the earth is pounded to powder, pounded and pounded﴾, pounded until you see in it no crookedness or elevation. The mountains are crushed, and there is no building, and no trees. The earth is stretched out like a leather hide, and the people will be upon it in one place; the caller will make them hear, and the sight will penetrate them. On this day ﴿man will remember, but how will the remembrance benefit him? (23) He will say: "O, would that I had sent forth for my life"﴾ [Al-Fajr 23-24]. But the time has passed. Yet today we are in the realm of action, in the time of respite, when a person can gain provision for his lasting abode, as the believer from the family of Pharaoh said: ﴿O my people, this worldly life is but a passing enjoyment, and indeed the Hereafter is the abode of settlement﴾ [Ghafir 39]. It is an enjoyment that a person takes pleasure in, just as a traveler enjoys the provisions of travel until his journey ends. So is this world.

Consider, my brother, consider what is to come by what has passed. All that has passed is as if it were an hour of a day. It is as though we were only just created. Likewise, what is to come will pass us swiftly and all of it will go by, and the journey ends at another place that is not a permanent dwelling: the graves, the tombs. Even so, they are not a place of settlement, because of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase diverts you (1) until you visit the graves﴾ [At-Takathur 1-2]. A Bedouin heard a man recite this verse and said: "By Allah, the visitor does not remain, and there must be a departure from this place." This is a strong deduction and a good understanding, supported by the many clear verses on this, such as the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then indeed, after that, you will surely die (15). Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, you will be resurrected﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 15-16].

Ibn 'Uthaymin's commentary on Surah 89, verse 22:

Allah, glorified and exalted, reminded of what will happen on this Day, so He said: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾ [Al-Fajr 22]. That is, row after row.

﴿Your Lord comes﴾. This coming is the coming of Allah Himself, mighty and majestic, because the verb is attributed to Allah. Every verb attributed to Allah is established for Him alone and not for anything else. This is the rule in the Arabic language and the rule regarding the names and attributes of Allah: whatever Allah attributes to Himself belongs to Himself and not to another. Accordingly, the One who comes is Allah, mighty and majestic, and not as those who deny the attributes distorted it when they said: "It is the command of Allah that comes." This is removing the speech from its apparent meaning without evidence. Our creed is to let the speech of Allah and His Messenger stand on its apparent meaning, without distorting it, and to say: Allah, exalted is He, will come on the Day of Resurrection Himself. But how is this coming? This is what we have no knowledge of. We do not know how He comes, and asking about such a thing is an innovation (bid'ah), as Imam Malik (may Allah have mercy on him) said when he was asked about the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿The Most Merciful settled upon the Throne﴾, "How did He settle?" A questioner asked, saying: "How did He settle?" That is, "What is the color of the settling?" Malik lowered his head until sweat (ruhada', meaning sweat) covered him, due to the severity of this question on his heart, because it is a grave question, the question of one who goes to extremes, of one who seeks to trouble, or of an innovator who intends harm. Then he raised his head and said: «The settling is not unknown, the how is not conceivable, belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation»[[Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (867) from Yahya ibn Yahya, who said: We were with Malik ibn Anas when a man came and said: "O Abu 'Abd Allah, ﴿The Most Merciful settled upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], how did He settle?" He said: Malik lowered his head until sweat covered him, then said: The settling is not unknown, the how is not conceivable, belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation, and I do not see you except as an innovator. He ordered that he be taken out.]]. The evidence is the final statement: «asking about it is an innovation». Consider this in all the attributes of Allah. If a questioner asked, saying: Allah says: ﴿What I created with My two hands﴾ [Sad 75], meaning Adam, how did He create him with His hands?

We say: this question is an innovation.

He says: I want knowledge; I do not like anything of my Lord's attributes to be hidden from me, so I want to know how He created him.

We say: We ask you easy questions. Are you more eager for knowledge than the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them?

Either he says yes, or he says no, and the expected answer is: no.

Alright, is the one to whom you directed the question more knowledgeable about the manner of Allah's attributes, or the Messenger, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon him?

He will say: the Messenger.

So the Companions were more eager for knowledge than you, and the one to whom the question is directed is more knowledgeable than the one you ask. Nevertheless, they did not ask, because they observe good manners with Allah, mighty and majestic, and they say in their hearts, and perhaps with their tongues: Allah is far too exalted and great for our understanding and intellects to encompass the modalities of His attributes. Allah, mighty and majestic, says in His Book regarding matters that are known by reason: ﴿And they do not encompass Him in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha 110], and regarding matters that are perceptible: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him, but He perceives vision﴾ [Al-An'am 103]. So we say: O brother, adhere to good manners. Do not ask how Allah created Adam with His hand; this is an innovation. Likewise with the rest of the attributes: if he asks how the eye of Allah, mighty and majestic, is, we say: this is an innovation. If he asks how the hand of Allah, mighty and majestic, is, we say: this is an innovation. You must adhere to good manners and not ask about the modality of the attributes of Allah, mighty and majestic.

Here, regarding the noble verse ﴿And your Lord comes﴾, when someone asks: How does He come? What do we say to him? Answer.

* A student: This is an innovation.

* The Shaykh: We say: this is an innovation. This is the rule; adhere to it. This question is an innovation, and every person who asks about the modality of Allah's attributes is an innovator who goes to extremes, asking about what cannot be reached. So our position regarding such a verse as ﴿And your Lord comes﴾ is to believe that Allah comes, but in what manner? Allah knows best.

Now, if someone said: Is it possible that His coming is like the coming of a human, or like the coming of a king to the place of a celebration?

The answer: No. We know that this does not occur. The evidence is the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [Ash-Shura 11]. So we know the negation and we do not know the affirmation; that is, we know that He cannot come in the manner of the coming of humans, but we do not affirm a modality. This is what is obligatory upon us.

As for His words: ﴿And the angels﴾, the definite article here ("al") is for generality; that is, all the angels come. They descend and surround the creation, the angels of the lowest heaven, then the angels of the second heaven, and so on, surrounding the creation to show greatness. Otherwise, creation cannot flee to the right or to the left. But to display the greatness of Allah and to make this great Day awe-inspiring, the angels descend and surround the creation. This is a witnessed Day, witnessed by the angels, humans, jinn, insects, and everything: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [At-Takwir 5]. It is a great Day that we do not comprehend now, nor can we imagine it, because it is greater than what can be imagined.

The third matter by which warning is given on this Day, after we have explained the first, which is the coming of Allah, and then the ranks of the angels, is His saying: ﴿And Hell will be brought forth on that Day﴾ [al-Fajr 23]. ﴿Brought forth on that Day﴾, and the one who brings it is not mentioned. But the Sunnah has shown that Hell will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand bridles, each bridle held by seventy thousand angels. [Narrated by Muslim (2842/29), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him.] And what will make you know the strength of the angels? It is a strength unlike the strength of humans or the strength of the jinn; rather, it is far greater, greater by a great deal. This is why, when an ʿifrit (a powerful jinn) among the jinn said to Solomon, ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾, regarding the throne of Bilqis, ﴿One who had knowledge from the Scripture said: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾ [an-Naml 39-40], and he saw it placed beside him. The scholars said: this man called upon Allah, and the angels carried it and brought it to Solomon in al-Sham from Yemen. So the strength of the angels is great, and they will drag this Fire with seventy thousand bridles, each bridle pulled by seventy thousand angels. So it is indeed great. We ask Allah for well-being, and we ask Allah to protect us and you from it. This Fire, ﴿when it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring﴾ [al-Furqan 12], meaning it sees its inhabitants. It is not like the roar of airplanes or machinery; it is a roar that tears hearts apart, and we seek refuge in Allah. ﴿Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them: Did no warner come to you?﴾ [al-Mulk 8]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, also said: ﴿It almost bursts with rage﴾ [al-Mulk 8], meaning it almost splits apart from the intensity of its rage against its inhabitants, and we seek refuge in Allah. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, has warned us of it. These three matters are all warnings: the coming of the Lord, Majestic is His majesty; the ranks of the angels; and third, the bringing forth of Hell.

﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ [al-Fajr 23]. ﴿Remember﴾ means be admonished. But how can he be admonished? The time has passed, and admonition has ended with the arrival of the appointed term in the world, before the human being reaches the Hereafter. ﴿Repentance is not for those who commit evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now," nor for those who die while they are disbelievers﴾ [an-Nisaʾ 18]. So we ask Allah, exalted is He, to make us and you among those who take admonition from His signs, and we ask Him, exalted is He, to grant us beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, and abundant good provision.

(...) It has been our custom to speak on what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes easy of the tafsir (exegesis) of the Noble Qur'an, and we have reached the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿He will say: "Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life!" On that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr 24-26], and this is the end of Surat al-Fajr.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ That is, when Allah comes on the Day of Resurrection, and the angels come in rows upon rows and surround the creation, and the terrors and frights occur, the human being will remember. He will remember that he was promised this Day, and that he was informed of it by the messengers, peace be upon them, who warned and gave fear. But whoever has the word of punishment decreed against him will not believe, even if every sign comes to him, and we seek refuge in Allah. Then he will remember. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿but how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ Where will remembrance be for him on this Day, when he has seen with certainty what he was told about? Faith born of witnessing does not benefit, because every person believes in what he has witnessed. The beneficial faith is belief in the unseen: ﴿those who believe in the unseen﴾ [al-Baqarah 3], so that one believes what the messengers reported from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and about the Last Day. On that Day the human being will remember, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿but how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ That is: it is far-fetched that he will benefit from this remembrance that has come to him when he witnessed the truth.

He will say, ﴿"Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life!"﴾ [Al-Fajr 24]. He wishes that he had sent forth (good deeds) for his life.

And what is his life? Do you think he means the life of this world? No, by Allah. The life of this world has ended and passed away. The life of this world is not truly life. In reality it is worries and troubles. Every clarity is followed by turbidity, every well-being is followed by sickness, and every gathering is followed by separation. Look at what has happened: where are the fathers? Where are the brothers? Where are the sons? Where are the spouses? Is this life? Never. For this reason, one of the wise poets said:

"There is no sweetness in living while its pleasures are clouded
by the remembrance of death and of old age."

Every person should remember that his end is one of two things: either death or decrepitude.

We know people who were young in the prime of youth, and they lived long, but they returned to the lowest state of old age. A person feels pity when he sees them, in a state of misery, even if they have the wealth and the family that they have. They are still in a state of misery. Likewise, every person either dies early, or he lives long and is returned to the lowest state of old age. So is this life?

Life is what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has explained: ﴿"Indeed, the Hereafter is the [true] life, if only they knew."﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 64]. That is, it is the complete life. He says this: ﴿"Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life!"﴾ He wishes, but it will not happen, ﴿"and how can the reminder [benefit] him?"﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 89, verse 25–30 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr 25, 26]. That is, on this Day, no one will punish as He punishes, and no one will bind as He binds. It is known that this disbeliever, (the believer will come to us, God willing), the disbeliever, no one will punish his punishment on that Day. And I will tell you why: because on the Standing (al-Mawqif) there will descend upon the people of the Fire a severe thirst. They will look at the Fire as though it were a mirage (al-sarab), and the mirage is what a person sees in the summer days, at the height of the heat, in the plains, until it appears to him as water. They will look at the Fire as though it were a mirage, and they will be thirsty, so they will rush toward it, hastening to it, desiring – what? – desiring to drink. But when they reach it, ﴿its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them: Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾ [al-Zumar 71]. The proof has been established against you. So they will rebuke them before they enter the Fire, and rebuke is a spiritual punishment and a psychological pain before they taste the pain of the Fire, and we seek refuge in Allah. May Allah protect me and you from it.

In the Fire, the Almighty, the Mighty and Majestic, will rebuke them with a rebuke greater than this. They will say: ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we will be wrongdoers﴾ [al-Mu'minun 106, 107]. Allah the Exalted, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, says: ﴿Remain in it with contempt, and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun 108]. What could be more eloquent than this humiliation, and we seek refuge in Allah! ﴿Remain in it with contempt and do not speak to Me﴾, said by the Most Merciful of the merciful. So who will have mercy on them after the Most Merciful? There is no one who will have mercy on them. The Prophet ﷺ has informed us «that the least punished of the people of the Fire is the one who has two sandals and two thongs of fire, from which his brain boils like a cauldron. He does not think that anyone is punished more severely than him, while he is the least punished of them» [[Muslim recorded it in his Sahih (213 / 364) with its chain from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «The least punished of the people of the Fire in punishment is the one who has two sandals and two thongs of fire, from which his brain boils like a cauldron boils. He does not see that anyone is more severely punished than him, and indeed he is the least of them in punishment».]]. The sandals are at the bottom of the body and the brain is at its top; so if the top of the body boils from its bottom, then the middle is all the more so. May Allah protect us and you from the Fire.

﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾, because they – and we seek refuge in Allah – will be bound; ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, thread him﴾ [al-Haqqah 32]. Put him into this chain, their hands are shackled. We ask Allah for well-being. No one can now imagine what they are in of misery, wretchedness and punishment. By Allah, a person sometimes wishes that he had not been created, out of fear of the Fire. «ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: Would that my mother had not borne me, and would that I were a tree that is cut down» [[The first part: "Would that my mother had not borne me" was recorded by Ibn Abi Shaybah (34480) as a saying of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him. As for the second part: "Would that I were a tree that is cut down," Ibn Abi Shaybah (34521) recorded it as a saying of Ibn Mas'ud, and Ahmad in al-Zuhd (786) recorded it as a saying of Abu Dhar, and Ibn Abi al-Dunya in al-Mutamanin (10) recorded it as a saying of Abu Bakr, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab (768) recorded it as a saying of Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with them all.]]. Because a person does not know: first, he does not know what state he is in now – is he upon what is right or upon what is wrong? Does his worship contain showing off? Does his worship contain innovation? Then he also does not see – and this is the most dangerous – what his end will be; «Indeed a man may work the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only a cubit, then the Decree overtakes him and he works the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6594) and Muslim (2643 / 1), from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. Who can feel safe at death, that he will not be turned away and led astray, and Satan comes to him saying: "I am your father, my son, leave Islam and be a Christian or a Jew"? Because some people – and we seek refuge in Allah – are tested at death; religions are presented to them and it is said: Choose Christianity, choose Judaism, turn away from Islam. And for this (...) "and from the trial of life and what?" And death. And who can feel safe? I ask Allah to make my end and yours good. Who can feel safe? So a person must prepare himself. ﴿He will say: Would that I had sent ahead for my life﴾ [al-Fajr 24]. ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾.

Then Allah concluded this surah with what gladdens the heart and expands the breast, saying: ﴿O soul at peace﴾. O Allah, make our souls at peace. ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾ [al-Fajr 27, 28]. ﴿Return to your Lord﴾ is said to a person at the moment of death, at the last instant of the world. It is said to his spirit: Go forth, O soul at peace, go forth to mercy from Allah and approval, and it rejoices, is delighted, and its departure from the body is made easy, because it has been given glad tidings of what is more pleasant than all of this world. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: «The place of a whip of one of you in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it» [[Recorded by al-Bukhari (3250) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. The whip (sawt) of a person is the short stick; the place of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and what is in it, and not your world only – the world from its beginning to its end, with what is in it of bliss, dominion and luxury and other things. The place of a whip is better than the world and what is in it. So how about one who looks over his kingdom a distance of two thousand years, two thousand years, seeing its farthest part as he sees its nearest! A bliss that we cannot grasp with our souls nor with our imagination; ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Sajdah 17].

The meaning of ﴿al-Mutma'innah﴾ is the believing one, the secure one; for you will not find a soul more tranquil than the soul of the believer, ever. The believer, my brothers, his soul is good and at peace. For this the Messenger ﷺ marvelled at the believer, saying: «How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for all his affairs are good; if hardship befalls him, he is patient and it is good for him, and if ease befalls him, he is grateful and it is good for him» [[Recorded by Muslim (2999) from the hadith of Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. He is at peace, walking with Allah in His decree and destiny, not angry at calamities, not arrogant at blessings, but thankful in blessings and patient in trials, so you find him at peace. But the disbeliever, or the one weak in faith, is not at peace; when affliction befalls him, he panics, becomes angry, and considers himself wronged by Allah – and we seek refuge in Allah – to the point that some of them commit suicide, they do not endure, they are not at peace, they are always in anxiety. He looks at himself and sees that he has little wealth, few dependents, no wife, no people to protect him, so he says: I am not in blessing, because so-and-so has wealth, has wives, has children, has a tribe that protects him, and I have none. So he does not see Allah's blessing upon him, because he is weak in faith, so he is not at peace, always in anxiety. For this we find people now going everywhere to entertain themselves, to remove pain and fatigue from themselves, but nothing removes that from you except what? Except true faith; it is what leads to tranquility. So the soul at peace is the believing one. What? The secure one: believing in this world, secure from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection. O Allah, make our souls like this.

O my brothers, some of the early generations (salaf) said a remarkable word: «If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, they would fight us for it with swords» [[The saying is of Ibrahim ibn Adham the ascetic, and al-Bayhaqi recorded it in al-Zuhd al-Kabir (80).]]. Do you find anyone more blessed in this world than the kings and their sons? Answer.
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: No, there is no one more blessed than them outwardly; i.e., the softness of the body or the comfort of the body. But their hearts are not like the hearts of the believers. The believer, who has nothing but a patched garment and a hut that does not protect him from rain or heat, yet is a believer, his worldly life and bliss are better than those of kings and the sons of kings; because his heart is illuminated by the light of Allah, by the light of faith.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, was imprisoned and harmed for the sake of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. When he was put into prison and the door was locked upon him, he, may Allah have mercy on him, said: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a gate; its inner side will contain mercy, and its outer side will be facing torment﴾ [al-Hadid 13]. He said this as a recounting of Allah's blessing, not as boasting. Then he said: What can my enemies do to me? What can they do?! Indeed my Paradise is in my breast. What is Paradise? Faith, knowledge and certainty. And my imprisonment is seclusion (khalwah), my exile – if they exile me from the land – is travel (siyahah), and my killing is martyrdom. Glory be to Allah! This is certainty, this is tranquility. If a person entered prison with us, he would be counting and calculating: what is my future! What is my children's future! My family! My people! This one says: my Paradise is in my breast. And he spoke the truth. Perhaps this is the secret in the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿They will not taste death therein except the first death﴾ [al-Dukhan 56]. That is, in Paradise ﴿they will not taste death therein except the first death﴾. It is known that Paradise has no death at all, neither first nor second. But since the bliss of the heart extends from this world to entering Paradise, the world and the Hereafter together become as though they were all Paradise, and there is only one death in them. So we ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make our end good, and to gather us and you and our Muslim brothers whom Allah has blessed in Paradise, from among the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, indeed He is over all things competent.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾. ﴿Well-pleased﴾ with what Allah has given you of bliss; ﴿pleasing﴾ in the sight of Allah the Mighty and Majestic; as He the Exalted said: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 119].

﴿So enter among My servants﴾ [al-Fajr 29], that is: enter among My righteous servants, be one of them; for the righteous servants of Allah are the best classes of mankind. Mankind has three classes: those upon whom favor is bestowed, those upon whom anger is incurred, and those who are astray. All these classes are mentioned in one surah. What is it?
* The students: al-Fatihah.
* The Shaykh: Surah al-Fatihah; ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray﴾ [al-Fatihah 6, 7].

And I ask you: when you recite this verse, does any of you feel that those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor are the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, and feel that he is asking Allah to guide him to the path of those?

Most people do not feel it; most people recite it like this, but do not feel that this is history; i.e., it refers to the history of nations.

As for the second class, ﴿those who have evoked [Allah's] anger﴾, they are the Jews and those like the Jews, from everyone who knew the truth and opposed it. Everyone who knew the truth and opposed it has in him a resemblance to the Jews, as Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: «Whoever among our scholars becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Jews» [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir (4/138) in his tafsir of Allah's saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [them] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah – give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [al-Tawbah 34].]].

(Those who are astray) are who? The Christians. They are those who were ignorant of the truth; they wanted it but were blinded to it, and we seek refuge in Allah; they were not guided to it. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: «And everyone of our worshippers who becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Christians» [[Ibid.]], because they – the worshippers – want good, they want worship, but they have no knowledge, so they are astray.

So I say, my brothers: people are of three classes: those upon whom favor is bestowed, those upon whom anger is incurred, and those who are astray.

And here He says: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾. Who are the servants? Which of the classes is intended? The first class, those upon whom favor is bestowed.

﴿And enter My Paradise﴾ [al-Fajr 30], His Paradise which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prepared for His friends. We ask Allah to make us and you among its people. He attributed it to Himself to honor it and magnify it, and to inform creation of His care for it, exalted is He. Allah, glorified and exalted, created it as a creation different from the creation of this world. He created for us in this world fruit, date palms and pomegranates; in Paradise there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates. Do you think that what is in Paradise is like what is in this world? Never; it is impossible, because Allah says: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [al-Sajdah 17]. And if what is in Paradise were like what is in this world, we would know it; it is similar in name, but not similar in reality or in how it is. For this He said: ﴿Enter My Paradise﴾, attributing it to Himself to indicate its nobility and Allah's care for it. This obliges a person to desire it with the utmost desire, just as he desires the houses of Allah, which are the mosques, because He attributed them to Himself; so likewise he should desire this abode which Allah attributed to Himself. The matter is easy; «A man said to the Messenger ﷺ: Guide me to a deed that will enter me into Paradise and keep me far from the Fire. He said: "You have asked about something great." It is indeed great; ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has certainly succeeded﴾ [Al 'Imran 185]. But «and indeed it is easy for whomever Allah makes it easy» – O Allah, make us easy for the ease – «it is easy for whomever Allah makes it easy: you worship Allah, associating nothing with Him, you establish prayer, and you pay zakah...»» [[Recorded by Ahmad (22016) from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, and he mentioned the hadith.]]. The main point is that the religion, praise be to Allah, is easy and simple, but it is the commanding souls (al-nufus al-ammarah bi'l-su') that come between us and our religion, and desires and doubts. ﴿Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah 201]. ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy; indeed You are the Bestower﴾ [Al 'Imran 8].

* * *

Allah the Exalted says: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿I swear by this city﴾ [al-Balad 1], ﴿and you are a resident in this city﴾ [al-Balad 2].

Another brief note on what was covered in the previous lesson, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr: 25–26]. I have recited it in this manner and explained it according to this reading, because there are two readings of the two aforementioned verses.

The first reading, which is in the Mushaf: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾. That is: no one punishes with the punishment of Allah; rather, the punishment of Allah is more severe. And no one binds with the binding of Allah; rather, His binding is more severe.

As for the reading ﴿So on that Day none will be punished with his punishment, and none will be bound with his binding﴾, meaning: no one is punished with the punishment of this man, nor is anyone bound with the binding of this man. This is the reading upon which we recited the verse and explained it, and for this reason the notice was given.

But since the bliss of the heart extends from this world to entering Paradise, the world and the Hereafter together become as though they were all Paradise, and there is only one death in them. So we ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make our end good, and to gather us and you and our Muslim brothers whom Allah has blessed in Paradise, from among the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, indeed He is over all things competent.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾. ﴿Well-pleased﴾ with what Allah has given you of bliss; ﴿pleasing﴾ in the sight of Allah the Mighty and Majestic; as He the Exalted said: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 119].

﴿So enter among My servants﴾ [al-Fajr 29], that is: enter among My righteous servants, be one of them; for the righteous servants of Allah are the best classes of mankind. Mankind has three classes: those upon whom favor is bestowed, those upon whom anger is incurred, and those who are astray. All these classes are mentioned in one surah. What is it?
* The students: al-Fatihah.
* The Shaykh: Surah al-Fatihah; ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray﴾ [al-Fatihah 6, 7].

And I ask you: when you recite this verse, does any of you feel that those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor are the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, and feel that he is asking Allah to guide him to the path of those?

Most people do not feel it; most people recite it like this, but do not feel that this is history; i.e., it refers to the history of nations.

As for the second class, ﴿those who have evoked [Allah's] anger﴾, they are the Jews and those like the Jews, from everyone who knew the truth and opposed it. Everyone who knew the truth and opposed it has in him a resemblance to the Jews, as Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: «Whoever among our scholars becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Jews» [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir (4/138) in his tafsir of Allah's saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [them] from the way of Allah. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: «And everyone of our worshippers who becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Christians» [[Ibid.]], because they – the worshippers – want good, they want worship, but they have no knowledge, so they are astray.

So I say, my brothers: people are of three classes: those upon whom favor is bestowed, those upon whom anger is incurred, and those who are astray.

And here He says: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾. Who are the servants? Which of the classes is intended? The first class, those upon whom favor is bestowed.

﴿And enter My Paradise﴾ [al-Fajr 30], His Paradise which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prepared for His friends. We ask Allah to make us and you among its people. He attributed it to Himself to honor it and magnify it, and to inform creation of His care for it, exalted is He. Allah, glorified and exalted, created it as a creation different from the creation of this world. He created for us in this world fruit, date palms and pomegranates; in Paradise there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates. Do you think that what is in Paradise is like what is in this world? Never; it is impossible, because Allah says: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [al-Sajdah 17]. And if what is in Paradise were like what is in this world, we would know it; it is similar in name, but not similar in reality or in how it is. For this He said: ﴿Enter My Paradise﴾, attributing it to Himself to indicate its nobility and Allah's care for it. This obliges a person to desire it with the utmost desire, just as he desires the houses of Allah, which are the mosques, because He attributed them to Himself; so likewise he should desire this abode which Allah attributed to Himself. The matter is easy; «A man said to the Messenger ﷺ: Guide me to a deed that will enter me into Paradise and keep me far from the Fire. He said: "You have asked about something great." It is indeed great; ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has certainly succeeded﴾ [Al 'Imran 185]. But «and indeed it is easy for whomever Allah makes it easy» – O Allah, make us easy for the ease – «it is easy for whomever Allah makes it easy: you worship Allah, associating nothing with Him, you establish prayer, and you pay zakah...»» [[Recorded by Ahmad (22016) from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, and he mentioned the hadith.]]. The main point is that the religion, praise be to Allah, is easy and simple, but it is the commanding souls (al-nufus al-ammarah bi'l-su') that come between us and our religion, and desires and doubts. ﴿Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah 201]. ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy; indeed You are the Bestower﴾ [Al 'Imran 8].

Allah the Exalted says: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿I swear by this city﴾ [al-Balad 1], ﴿and you are a resident in this city﴾ [al-Balad 2].

Another brief note on what was covered in the previous lesson, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr: 25–26]. I have recited it in this manner and explained it according to this reading, because there are two readings of the two aforementioned verses.

The first reading, which is in the Mushaf: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾. That is: no one punishes with the punishment of Allah; rather, the punishment of Allah is more severe. And no one binds with the binding of Allah; rather, His binding is more severe.

As for the reading ﴿So on that Day none will be punished with his punishment, and none will be bound with his binding﴾, meaning: no one is punished with the punishment of this man, nor is anyone bound with the binding of this man. That is, on this Day, no one will punish as He punishes, and no one will bind as He binds. It is known that this disbeliever, (the believer will come to us, God willing), the disbeliever, no one will punish his punishment on that Day. And I will tell you why: because on the Standing (al-Mawqif) there will descend upon the people of the Fire a severe thirst. They will look at the Fire as though it were a mirage (al-sarab), and the mirage is what a person sees in the summer days, at the height of the heat, in the plains, until it appears to him as water. They will look at the Fire as though it were a mirage, and they will be thirsty, so they will rush toward it, hastening to it, desiring – what? – desiring to drink. But when they reach it, ﴿its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them: Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾ [al-Zumar 71]. The sandals are at the bottom of the body and the brain is at its top; so if the top of the body boils from its bottom, then the middle is all the more so. ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾, because they – and we seek refuge in Allah – will be bound; ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, thread him﴾ [al-Haqqah 32]. Put him into this chain, their hands are shackled. We ask Allah for well-being. No one can now imagine what they are in of misery, wretchedness and punishment. Then Allah concluded this surah with what gladdens the heart and expands the breast, saying: ﴿O soul at peace﴾. O Allah, make our souls at peace. ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾ [al-Fajr 27, 28]. ﴿Return to your Lord﴾ is said to a person at the moment of death, at the last instant of the world. It is said to his spirit: Go forth, O soul at peace, go forth to mercy from Allah and approval, and it rejoices, is delighted, and its departure from the body is made easy, because it has been given glad tidings of what is more pleasant than all of this world. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: «The place of a whip of one of you in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it» [[Recorded by al-Bukhari (3250) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. The whip (sawt) of a person is the short stick; the place of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and what is in it, and not your world only – the world from its beginning to its end, with what is in it of bliss, dominion and luxury and other things. The place of a whip is better than the world and what is in it. So how about one who looks over his kingdom a distance of two thousand years, two thousand years, seeing its farthest part as he sees its nearest! A bliss that we cannot grasp with our souls nor with our imagination; ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Sajdah 17].

The meaning of ﴿al-Mutma'innah﴾ is the believing one, the secure one; for you will not find a soul more tranquil than the soul of the believer, ever. For this the Messenger ﷺ marvelled at the believer, saying: «How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for all his affairs are good; if hardship befalls him, he is patient and it is good for him, and if ease befalls him, he is grateful and it is good for him» [[Recorded by Muslim (2999) from the hadith of Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. He is at peace, walking with Allah in His decree and destiny, not angry at calamities, not arrogant at blessings, but thankful in blessings and patient in trials, so you find him at peace. But the disbeliever, or the one weak in faith, is not at peace; when affliction befalls him, he panics, becomes angry, and considers himself wronged by Allah – and we seek refuge in Allah – to the point that some of them commit suicide, they do not endure, they are not at peace, they are always in anxiety. He looks at himself and sees that he has little wealth, few dependents, no wife, no people to protect him, so he says: I am not in blessing, because so-and-so has wealth, has wives, has children, has a tribe that protects him, and I have none. So he does not see Allah's blessing upon him, because he is weak in faith, so he is not at peace, always in anxiety. For this we find people now going everywhere to entertain themselves, to remove pain and fatigue from themselves, but nothing removes that from you except what? Except true faith; it is what leads to tranquility. So the soul at peace is the believing one. What? The secure one: believing in this world, secure from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection. O Allah, make our souls like this.

O my brothers, some of the early generations (salaf) said a remarkable word: «If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, they would fight us for it with swords» [[The saying is of Ibrahim ibn Adham the ascetic, and al-Bayhaqi recorded it in al-Zuhd al-Kabir (80).]]. * The students: No.
* The Shaykh: No, there is no one more blessed than them outwardly; i.e., the softness of the body or the comfort of the body. But their hearts are not like the hearts of the believers. He said this as a recounting of Allah's blessing, not as boasting. Then he said: What can my enemies do to me? What can they do?! Indeed my Paradise is in my breast. What is Paradise? Faith, knowledge and certainty. And my imprisonment is seclusion (khalwah), my exile – if they exile me from the land – is travel (siyahah), and my killing is martyrdom. Glory be to Allah! This is certainty, this is tranquility. If a person entered prison with us, he would be counting and calculating: what is my future! What is my children's future! My family! My people! And here He says: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾. Who are the servants? Which of the classes is intended? The first class, those upon whom favor is bestowed.
