Who can feel safe at death, that he will not be turned away and led astray, and Satan comes to him saying: "I am your father, my son, leave Islam and be a Christian or a Jew"? Because some people – and we seek refuge in Allah – are tested at death; religions are presented to them and it is said: Choose Christianity, choose Judaism, turn away from Islam. And for this (...) "and from the trial of life and what?" And death. And who can feel safe? I ask Allah to make my end and yours good. Who can feel safe? So a person must prepare himself. ﴿He will say: Would that I had sent ahead for my life﴾ [al-Fajr 24]. ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾.

Then Allah concluded this surah with what gladdens the heart and expands the breast, saying: ﴿O soul at peace﴾. O Allah, make our souls at peace. ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾ [al-Fajr 27, 28]. ﴿Return to your Lord﴾ is said to a person at the moment of death, at the last instant of the world. It is said to his spirit: Go forth, O soul at peace, go forth to mercy from Allah and approval, and it rejoices, is delighted, and its departure from the body is made easy, because it has been given glad tidings of what is more pleasant than all of this world. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: «The place of a whip of one of you in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it» [[Recorded by al-Bukhari (3250) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. The whip (sawt) of a person is the short stick; the place of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and what is in it, and not your world only – the world from its beginning to its end, with what is in it of bliss, dominion and luxury and other things. The place of a whip is better than the world and what is in it. So how about one who looks over his kingdom a distance of two thousand years, two thousand years, seeing its farthest part as he sees its nearest! A bliss that we cannot grasp with our souls nor with our imagination; ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Sajdah 17].

The meaning of ﴿al-Mutma'innah﴾ is the believing one, the secure one; for you will not find a soul more tranquil than the soul of the believer, ever. The believer, my brothers, his soul is good and at peace. For this the Messenger ﷺ marvelled at the believer, saying: «How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for all his affairs are good; if hardship befalls him, he is patient and it is good for him, and if ease befalls him, he is grateful and it is good for him» [[Recorded by Muslim (2999) from the hadith of Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. He is at peace, walking with Allah in His decree and destiny, not angry at calamities, not arrogant at blessings, but thankful in blessings and patient in trials, so you find him at peace. But the disbeliever, or the one weak in faith, is not at peace; when affliction befalls him, he panics, becomes angry, and considers himself wronged by Allah – and we seek refuge in Allah – to the point that some of them commit suicide, they do not endure, they are not at peace, they are always in anxiety. He looks at himself and sees that he has little wealth, few dependents, no wife, no people to protect him, so he says: I am not in blessing, because so-and-so has wealth, has wives, has children, has a tribe that protects him, and I have none. So he does not see Allah's blessing upon him, because he is weak in faith, so he is not at peace, always in anxiety. For this we find people now going everywhere to entertain themselves, to remove pain and fatigue from themselves, but nothing removes that from you except what? Except true faith; it is what leads to tranquility. So the soul at peace is the believing one. What? The secure one: believing in this world, secure from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection. O Allah, make our souls like this.

O my brothers, some of the early generations (salaf) said a remarkable word: «If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, they would fight us for it with swords» [[The saying is of Ibrahim ibn Adham the ascetic, and al-Bayhaqi recorded it in al-Zuhd al-Kabir (80).]]. Do you find anyone more blessed in this world than the kings and their sons? Answer.
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: No, there is no one more blessed than them outwardly; i.e., the softness of the body or the comfort of the body. But their hearts are not like the hearts of the believers. The believer, who has nothing but a patched garment and a hut that does not protect him from rain or heat, yet is a believer, his worldly life and bliss are better than those of kings and the sons of kings; because his heart is illuminated by the light of Allah, by the light of faith.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, was imprisoned and harmed for the sake of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. When he was put into prison and the door was locked upon him, he, may Allah have mercy on him, said: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a gate; its inner side will contain mercy, and its outer side will be facing torment﴾ [al-Hadid 13]. He said this as a recounting of Allah's blessing, not as boasting. Then he said: What can my enemies do to me? What can they do?! Indeed my Paradise is in my breast. What is Paradise? Faith, knowledge and certainty. And my imprisonment is seclusion (khalwah), my exile – if they exile me from the land – is travel (siyahah), and my killing is martyrdom. Glory be to Allah! This is certainty, this is tranquility. If a person entered prison with us, he would be counting and calculating: what is my future! What is my children's future! My family! My people! This one says: my Paradise is in my breast. And he spoke the truth. Perhaps this is the secret in the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿They will not taste death therein except the first death﴾ [al-Dukhan 56]. That is, in Paradise ﴿they will not taste death therein except the first death﴾. It is known that Paradise has no death at all, neither first nor second. But since the bliss of the heart extends from this world to entering Paradise, the world and the Hereafter together become as though they were all Paradise, and there is only one death in them. So we ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make our end good, and to gather us and you and our Muslim brothers whom Allah has blessed in Paradise, from among the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, indeed He is over all things competent.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾. ﴿Well-pleased﴾ with what Allah has given you of bliss; ﴿pleasing﴾ in the sight of Allah the Mighty and Majestic; as He the Exalted said: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 119].

﴿So enter among My servants﴾ [al-Fajr 29], that is: enter among My righteous servants, be one of them; for the righteous servants of Allah are the best classes of mankind. Mankind has three classes: those upon whom favor is bestowed, those upon whom anger is incurred, and those who are astray. All these classes are mentioned in one surah. What is it?
* The students: al-Fatihah.
* The Shaykh: Surah al-Fatihah; ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray﴾ [al-Fatihah 6, 7].

And I ask you: when you recite this verse, does any of you feel that those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor are the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, and feel that he is asking Allah to guide him to the path of those?

Most people do not feel it; most people recite it like this, but do not feel that this is history; i.e., it refers to the history of nations.

As for the second class, ﴿those who have evoked [Allah's] anger﴾, they are the Jews and those like the Jews, from everyone who knew the truth and opposed it. Everyone who knew the truth and opposed it has in him a resemblance to the Jews, as Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: «Whoever among our scholars becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Jews» [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir (4/138) in his tafsir of Allah's saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [them] from the way of Allah. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: «And everyone of our worshippers who becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Christians» [[Ibid.]], because they – the worshippers – want good, they want worship, but they have no knowledge, so they are astray.

So I say, my brothers: people are of three classes: those upon whom favor is bestowed, those upon whom anger is incurred, and those who are astray.

And here He says: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾. Who are the servants? Which of the classes is intended? The first class, those upon whom favor is bestowed.

﴿And enter My Paradise﴾ [al-Fajr 30], His Paradise which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prepared for His friends. We ask Allah to make us and you among its people. He attributed it to Himself to honor it and magnify it, and to inform creation of His care for it, exalted is He. Allah, glorified and exalted, created it as a creation different from the creation of this world. He created for us in this world fruit, date palms and pomegranates; in Paradise there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates. Do you think that what is in Paradise is like what is in this world? Never; it is impossible, because Allah says: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [al-Sajdah 17]. And if what is in Paradise were like what is in this world, we would know it; it is similar in name, but not similar in reality or in how it is. For this He said: ﴿Enter My Paradise﴾, attributing it to Himself to indicate its nobility and Allah's care for it. The main point is that the religion, praise be to Allah, is easy and simple, but it is the commanding souls (al-nufus al-ammarah bi'l-su') that come between us and our religion, and desires and doubts. ﴿Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah 201]. ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy; indeed You are the Bestower﴾ [Al 'Imran 8].

Allah the Exalted says: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿I swear by this city﴾ [al-Balad 1], ﴿and you are a resident in this city﴾ [al-Balad 2].

Another brief note on what was covered in the previous lesson, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr: 25–26]. I have recited it in this manner and explained it according to this reading, because there are two readings of the two aforementioned verses.

The first reading, which is in the Mushaf: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾. That is: no one punishes with the punishment of Allah; rather, the punishment of Allah is more severe. And no one binds with the binding of Allah; rather, His binding is more severe.

As for the reading ﴿So on that Day none will be punished with his punishment, and none will be bound with his binding﴾, meaning: no one is punished with the punishment of this man, nor is anyone bound with the binding of this man. This is the reading upon which we recited the verse and explained it, and for this reason the notice was given.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 89, verse 25–30 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr 25, 26]. That is, on this Day, no one will punish as He punishes, and no one will bind as He binds. It is known that this disbeliever, (the believer will come to us, God willing), the disbeliever, no one will punish his punishment on that Day. And I will tell you why: because on the Standing (al-Mawqif) there will descend upon the people of the Fire a severe thirst. They will look at the Fire as though it were a mirage (al-sarab), and the mirage is what a person sees in the summer days, at the height of the heat, in the plains, until it appears to him as water. They will look at the Fire as though it were a mirage, and they will be thirsty, so they will rush toward it, hastening to it, desiring – what? – desiring to drink. But when they reach it, ﴿its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them: Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾ [al-Zumar 71]. The proof has been established against you. So they will rebuke them before they enter the Fire, and rebuke is a spiritual punishment and a psychological pain before they taste the pain of the Fire, and we seek refuge in Allah. May Allah protect me and you from it.

In the Fire, the Almighty, the Mighty and Majestic, will rebuke them with a rebuke greater than this. They will say: ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we will be wrongdoers﴾ [al-Mu'minun 106, 107]. Allah the Exalted, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, says: ﴿Remain in it with contempt, and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun 108]. What could be more eloquent than this humiliation, and we seek refuge in Allah! ﴿Remain in it with contempt and do not speak to Me﴾, said by the Most Merciful of the merciful. So who will have mercy on them after the Most Merciful? There is no one who will have mercy on them. The Prophet ﷺ has informed us «that the least punished of the people of the Fire is the one who has two sandals and two thongs of fire, from which his brain boils like a cauldron. The sandals are at the bottom of the body and the brain is at its top; so if the top of the body boils from its bottom, then the middle is all the more so. ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾, because they – and we seek refuge in Allah – will be bound; ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, thread him﴾ [al-Haqqah 32]. Allah the Exalted says: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿I swear by this city﴾ [al-Balad 1], ﴿and you are a resident in this city﴾ [al-Balad 2].

Another brief note on what was covered in the previous lesson, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr: 25–26]. I have recited it in this manner and explained it according to this reading, because there are two readings of the two aforementioned verses.

The first reading, which is in the Mushaf: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾. That is: no one punishes with the punishment of Allah; rather, the punishment of Allah is more severe. And no one binds with the binding of Allah; rather, His binding is more severe.

As for the reading ﴿So on that Day none will be punished with his punishment, and none will be bound with his binding﴾, meaning: no one is punished with the punishment of this man, nor is anyone bound with the binding of this man. This is the reading upon which we recited the verse and explained it, and for this reason the notice was given.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 89, verse 25–30 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr 25, 26]. That is, on this Day, no one will punish as He punishes, and no one will bind as He binds. It is known that this disbeliever, (the believer will come to us, God willing), the disbeliever, no one will punish his punishment on that Day. And I will tell you why: because on the Standing (al-Mawqif) there will descend upon the people of the Fire a severe thirst. They will look at the Fire as though it were a mirage (al-sarab), and the mirage is what a person sees in the summer days, at the height of the heat, in the plains, until it appears to him as water. They will look at the Fire as though it were a mirage, and they will be thirsty, so they will rush toward it, hastening to it, desiring – what? – desiring to drink. But when they reach it, ﴿its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them: Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾ [al-Zumar 71]. The proof has been established against you. So they will rebuke them before they enter the Fire, and rebuke is a spiritual punishment and a psychological pain before they taste the pain of the Fire, and we seek refuge in Allah. May Allah protect me and you from it.

In the Fire, the Almighty, the Mighty and Majestic, will rebuke them with a rebuke greater than this. They will say: ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we will be wrongdoers﴾ [al-Mu'minun 106, 107]. Allah the Exalted, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, says: ﴿Remain in it with contempt, and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun 108]. What could be more eloquent than this humiliation, and we seek refuge in Allah! ﴿Remain in it with contempt and do not speak to Me﴾, said by the Most Merciful of the merciful. So who will have mercy on them after the Most Merciful? There is no one who will have mercy on them. The Prophet ﷺ has informed us «that the least punished of the people of the Fire is the one who has two sandals and two thongs of fire, from which his brain boils like a cauldron. He does not think that anyone is punished more severely than him, while he is the least punished of them» [[Muslim recorded it in his Sahih (213 / 364) with its chain from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «The least punished of the people of the Fire in punishment is the one who has two sandals and two thongs of fire, from which his brain boils like a cauldron boils. He does not see that anyone is more severely punished than him, and indeed he is the least of them in punishment».]]. The sandals are at the bottom of the body and the brain is at its top; so if the top of the body boils from its bottom, then the middle is all the more so. May Allah protect us and you from the Fire.

﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾, because they – and we seek refuge in Allah – will be bound; ﴿Then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, thread him﴾ [al-Haqqah 32]. Put him into this chain, their hands are shackled. We ask Allah for well-being. No one can now imagine what they are in of misery, wretchedness and punishment. By Allah, a person sometimes wishes that he had not been created, out of fear of the Fire. «ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: Would that my mother had not borne me, and would that I were a tree that is cut down» [[The first part: "Would that my mother had not borne me" was recorded by Ibn Abi Shaybah (34480) as a saying of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him. As for the second part: "Would that I were a tree that is cut down," Ibn Abi Shaybah (34521) recorded it as a saying of Ibn Mas'ud, and Ahmad in al-Zuhd (786) recorded it as a saying of Abu Dhar, and Ibn Abi al-Dunya in al-Mutamanin (10) recorded it as a saying of Abu Bakr, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab (768) recorded it as a saying of Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with them all.]]. Because a person does not know: first, he does not know what state he is in now – is he upon what is right or upon what is wrong? Does his worship contain showing off? Does his worship contain innovation? Then he also does not see – and this is the most dangerous – what his end will be; «Indeed a man may work the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only a cubit, then the Decree overtakes him and he works the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6594) and Muslim (2643 / 1), from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. Who can feel safe at death, that he will not be turned away and led astray, and Satan comes to him saying: "I am your father, my son, leave Islam and be a Christian or a Jew"? Because some people – and we seek refuge in Allah – are tested at death; religions are presented to them and it is said: Choose Christianity, choose Judaism, turn away from Islam. And for this (...) "and from the trial of life and what?" And death. And who can feel safe? I ask Allah to make my end and yours good. Who can feel safe? So a person must prepare himself. ﴿He will say: Would that I had sent ahead for my life﴾ [al-Fajr 24]. ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾.

Then Allah concluded this surah with what gladdens the heart and expands the breast, saying: ﴿O soul at peace﴾. O Allah, make our souls at peace. ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾ [al-Fajr 27, 28]. ﴿Return to your Lord﴾ is said to a person at the moment of death, at the last instant of the world. It is said to his spirit: Go forth, O soul at peace, go forth to mercy from Allah and approval, and it rejoices, is delighted, and its departure from the body is made easy, because it has been given glad tidings of what is more pleasant than all of this world. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: «The place of a whip of one of you in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it» [[Recorded by al-Bukhari (3250) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. The whip (sawt) of a person is the short stick; the place of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and what is in it, and not your world only – the world from its beginning to its end, with what is in it of bliss, dominion and luxury and other things. The place of a whip is better than the world and what is in it. So how about one who looks over his kingdom a distance of two thousand years, two thousand years, seeing its farthest part as he sees its nearest! A bliss that we cannot grasp with our souls nor with our imagination; ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Sajdah 17].

The meaning of ﴿al-Mutma'innah﴾ is the believing one, the secure one; for you will not find a soul more tranquil than the soul of the believer, ever. The believer, my brothers, his soul is good and at peace. For this the Messenger ﷺ marvelled at the believer, saying: «How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for all his affairs are good; if hardship befalls him, he is patient and it is good for him, and if ease befalls him, he is grateful and it is good for him» [[Recorded by Muslim (2999) from the hadith of Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. He is at peace, walking with Allah in His decree and destiny, not angry at calamities, not arrogant at blessings, but thankful in blessings and patient in trials, so you find him at peace. But the disbeliever, or the one weak in faith, is not at peace; when affliction befalls him, he panics, becomes angry, and considers himself wronged by Allah – and we seek refuge in Allah – to the point that some of them commit suicide, they do not endure, they are not at peace, they are always in anxiety. He looks at himself and sees that he has little wealth, few dependents, no wife, no people to protect him, so he says: I am not in blessing, because so-and-so has wealth, has wives, has children, has a tribe that protects him, and I have none. So he does not see Allah's blessing upon him, because he is weak in faith, so he is not at peace, always in anxiety. For this we find people now going everywhere to entertain themselves, to remove pain and fatigue from themselves, but nothing removes that from you except what? Except true faith; it is what leads to tranquility. So the soul at peace is the believing one. What? The secure one: believing in this world, secure from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection. O Allah, make our souls like this.

O my brothers, some of the early generations (salaf) said a remarkable word: «If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, they would fight us for it with swords» [[The saying is of Ibrahim ibn Adham the ascetic, and al-Bayhaqi recorded it in al-Zuhd al-Kabir (80).]]. Do you find anyone more blessed in this world than the kings and their sons? Answer.
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: No, there is no one more blessed than them outwardly; i.e., the softness of the body or the comfort of the body. But their hearts are not like the hearts of the believers. The believer, who has nothing but a patched garment and a hut that does not protect him from rain or heat, yet is a believer, his worldly life and bliss are better than those of kings and the sons of kings; because his heart is illuminated by the light of Allah, by the light of faith.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, was imprisoned and harmed for the sake of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. When he was put into prison and the door was locked upon him, he, may Allah have mercy on him, said: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a gate; its inner side will contain mercy, and its outer side will be facing torment﴾ [al-Hadid 13]. He said this as a recounting of Allah's blessing, not as boasting. Then he said: What can my enemies do to me? What can they do?! Indeed my Paradise is in my breast. What is Paradise? Faith, knowledge and certainty. And my imprisonment is seclusion (khalwah), my exile – if they exile me from the land – is travel (siyahah), and my killing is martyrdom. Glory be to Allah! This is certainty, this is tranquility. If a person entered prison with us, he would be counting and calculating: what is my future! What is my children's future! My family! My people! This one says: my Paradise is in my breast. And he spoke the truth. Perhaps this is the secret in the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿They will not taste death therein except the first death﴾ [al-Dukhan 56]. That is, in Paradise ﴿they will not taste death therein except the first death﴾. It is known that Paradise has no death at all, neither first nor second. But since the bliss of the heart extends from this world to entering Paradise, the world and the Hereafter together become as though they were all Paradise, and there is only one death in them. So we ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make our end good, and to gather us and you and our Muslim brothers whom Allah has blessed in Paradise, from among the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, indeed He is over all things competent.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾. ﴿Well-pleased﴾ with what Allah has given you of bliss; ﴿pleasing﴾ in the sight of Allah the Mighty and Majestic; as He the Exalted said: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 119].

﴿So enter among My servants﴾ [al-Fajr 29], that is: enter among My righteous servants, be one of them; for the righteous servants of Allah are the best classes of mankind. Mankind has three classes: those upon whom favor is bestowed, those upon whom anger is incurred, and those who are astray. All these classes are mentioned in one surah. What is it?
* The students: al-Fatihah.
* The Shaykh: Surah al-Fatihah; ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray﴾ [al-Fatihah 6, 7].

And I ask you: when you recite this verse, does any of you feel that those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor are the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, and feel that he is asking Allah to guide him to the path of those?

Most people do not feel it; most people recite it like this, but do not feel that this is history; i.e., it refers to the history of nations.

As for the second class, ﴿those who have evoked [Allah's] anger﴾, they are the Jews and those like the Jews, from everyone who knew the truth and opposed it. Everyone who knew the truth and opposed it has in him a resemblance to the Jews, as Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: «Whoever among our scholars becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Jews» [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir (4/138) in his tafsir of Allah's saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [them] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah – give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [al-Tawbah 34].]].

(Those who are astray) are who? The Christians. They are those who were ignorant of the truth; they wanted it but were blinded to it, and we seek refuge in Allah; they were not guided to it. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: «And everyone of our worshippers who becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Christians» [[Ibid.]], because they – the worshippers – want good, they want worship, but they have no knowledge, so they are astray.

So I say, my brothers: people are of three classes: those upon whom favor is bestowed, those upon whom anger is incurred, and those who are astray.

And here He says: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾. Who are the servants? Which of the classes is intended? The first class, those upon whom favor is bestowed.

﴿And enter My Paradise﴾ [al-Fajr 30], His Paradise which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prepared for His friends. We ask Allah to make us and you among its people. He attributed it to Himself to honor it and magnify it, and to inform creation of His care for it, exalted is He. Allah, glorified and exalted, created it as a creation different from the creation of this world. He created for us in this world fruit, date palms and pomegranates; in Paradise there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates. Do you think that what is in Paradise is like what is in this world? Never; it is impossible, because Allah says: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [al-Sajdah 17]. And if what is in Paradise were like what is in this world, we would know it; it is similar in name, but not similar in reality or in how it is. For this He said: ﴿Enter My Paradise﴾, attributing it to Himself to indicate its nobility and Allah's care for it. This obliges a person to desire it with the utmost desire, just as he desires the houses of Allah, which are the mosques, because He attributed them to Himself; so likewise he should desire this abode which Allah attributed to Himself. The matter is easy; «A man said to the Messenger ﷺ: Guide me to a deed that will enter me into Paradise and keep me far from the Fire. He said: "You have asked about something great." It is indeed great; ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has certainly succeeded﴾ [Al 'Imran 185]. But «and indeed it is easy for whomever Allah makes it easy» – O Allah, make us easy for the ease – «it is easy for whomever Allah makes it easy: you worship Allah, associating nothing with Him, you establish prayer, and you pay zakah...»» [[Recorded by Ahmad (22016) from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, and he mentioned the hadith.]]. The main point is that the religion, praise be to Allah, is easy and simple, but it is the commanding souls (al-nufus al-ammarah bi'l-su') that come between us and our religion, and desires and doubts. ﴿Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah 201]. ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy; indeed You are the Bestower﴾ [Al 'Imran 8].
